body:
After having a previous good trip with Morning Glory seeds, I wanted to increase the dosage and introduce my friend to them. We are both experienced trippers, having experimented many times with mushrooms, LSD, mescaline, 2CE and 2CB.
We each divided up [roughly] 500 hundred seeds between us, and simply chewed and swallowed them. This took a long time, but luckily the seeds arent in the peyote league taste wise.
As before the LSA takes 3 or 4 hours to kick in (would likely be much quicker if one prepared them in a drink). Initially the seeds are heavily sedating, they make me just want to lie down. There was no nausea however, probably due to marijuana that was both smoked and consumed in some potent space cakes.
Hours later the euphoria began to kick in, intense, giggly, like acid. The world had taken on a milky hue, and there were detailed open eyed visuals. These were greatly vamped up with marijuana. Sensory muddling and time loops were obvious, just like on acid. Socialising with relatively sober adults is a bit of a challenge on these seeds. Like all psychedelics I prefer to be in the company of fellow trippers.
We went for a walk when it was dark, and the intensity and the colours I was seeing were impressive. I had these intense surges I would call them in my head, not pleasant, that came in waves. These only seemed apparent after having 2 hits of marijuana, and they didnt last long. My friend was also tripping heavily, despite not having had any marijuana for hours. On this walk (on a country road at night) he had a vivid flashback of a car crash he had many years before. This only lasted a few seconds, but he said if affected the rest of the trip. He didnt tell me about this until a week later, not wanting to affect my trip-I would much rather have known there and then though. The trip is long lasting, especially with the marijuana. We ate the seeds around 5 and I was still tripping nicely at 1 in the morning.
All in all an interesting and worthwhile experience, and 1 that I definitely will be repeating.
